requirements:
R1. Implement exact rational arithmetic in Rust as a SINGLE source file that compiles with `rustc --edition 2024`, using std only. Output ONLY the Rust source code inside ```rust fences. No main function is required. Do not use inner attributes or inner documentation comments.

R2. Expose `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] pub struct Rational` with private fields, and the following public inherent methods: `pub fn new(num: i64, den: i64) -> Result<Self, RationalError>`, `pub fn numerator(&self) -> i64`, `pub fn denominator(&self) -> i64`, `pub fn add(&self, rhs: &Self) -> Result<Self, RationalError>`, `pub fn sub(&self, rhs: &Self) -> Result<Self, RationalError>`, `pub fn mul(&self, rhs: &Self) -> Result<Self, RationalError>`, `pub fn div(&self, rhs: &Self) -> Result<Self, RationalError>`, `pub fn neg(&self) -> Result<Self, RationalError>`, and `pub fn parse(text: &str) -> Result<Self, RationalError>`. Implement `std::fmt::Display` for Rational.

R3. Expose `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] pub enum ParseKind { Empty, InvalidByte, NonCanonical, OutOfRange, ZeroDenominator }` and `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] pub enum RationalError { ZeroDenominator, DivideByZero, Overflow, Parse { at: usize, kind: ParseKind } }`. Error fields and variants are exactly as shown.

R4. Every successful Rational is reduced by the positive greatest common divisor, has a positive denominator in 1..=i64::MAX and a numerator in i64::MIN..=i64::MAX, and represents zero as 0/1. Equal values compare equal.

R5. new first rejects den == 0 with RationalError::ZeroDenominator, even if num == 0. Otherwise normalize the mathematical fraction before checking the normalized bounds; negative denominators flip the sign. Zero with any nonzero denominator succeeds. A normalized numerator or denominator outside R4 returns RationalError::Overflow. In particular, support i64::MIN inputs without wrapping or panicking.

R6. add, sub, mul and div compute the mathematical result, fully reduce it, then return Overflow only if its normalized representation exceeds R4. A large unreduced intermediate is not by itself an error. sub must not require negating its rhs as a separate bounded Rational operation.

R7. div checks a zero rhs numerator first and returns DivideByZero (including 0 divided by 0). neg returns the exact negative or Overflow; negating i64::MIN/1 overflows. No method changes its operands.

R8. Display uses base-10 ASCII with no spaces or plus sign: just the numerator if denominator is 1, otherwise numerator/denominator. There is no leading zero except the single zero, and no negative zero. Parsing Display output must recover the same value.

R9. parse is strict: first validate the entire byte grammar `-?[0-9]+(/[0-9]+)?`. Only an ASCII minus at byte 0 is allowed. Empty text returns Parse { at: 0, kind: Empty }. On nonempty input, the first byte violating this grammar returns InvalidByte at its byte offset. If a required digit is absent at end, the offset is text.len(). Byte offsets refer to UTF-8 bytes, not characters. A second slash, whitespace, plus, or sign in a denominator is invalid.

R10. After full syntax validation, run the checks R11 through R16 in the listed order; the first failed check wins. Syntax errors always win over magnitude and canonicality errors anywhere in the text. parse never normalizes noncanonical text.

R11. First reject a numerator with two or more digits whose first digit is 0, with NonCanonical at the second numerator digit (offset 1 for unsigned, 2 for negative). Next reject the exact numerator token -0 with NonCanonical at 0. Next reject a denominator with two or more digits whose first digit is 0, with NonCanonical at its second digit.

R12. Next check the numerator magnitude against i64::MAX for unsigned text or 2^63 for negative text. Failure is OutOfRange at offset 0, including arbitrarily long digit sequences. The exact negative magnitude 2^63 is valid.

R13. Next, if a denominator is present, check its magnitude against i64::MAX. Failure is OutOfRange at the first denominator digit, even if a later mathematical reduction could make the fraction fit.

R14. Next reject a denominator token 0 with ZeroDenominator at its digit offset. This parse error is wrapped in RationalError::Parse, unlike new's ZeroDenominator.

R15. Next reject denominator 1 with NonCanonical at the slash offset. Next reject a zero numerator with an explicit fraction with NonCanonical at the slash offset.

R16. Finally reject a fraction whose numerator absolute value and denominator have gcd greater than 1, with NonCanonical at the slash offset. All remaining grammar-valid text succeeds. Bare integers are valid, including 0 and i64::MIN.
